title: The estimator companion: when a share of a benchmark number is estimable, and why here it is not
one_line: An estimator paper. It gives the exact condition under which two standard routes to a mediated fraction agree, shows by calibration against an injected known truth that here neither is readable, withdraws every mediated fraction it previously reported, and prices two covariate channels directly instead.
abstract_as_printed: On a corpus written by design programs, a benchmark number is carried by a covariate somebody chose, and the work is to price each choice. This paper supplies what pricing needs and cannot assume: the condition under which a share of that number is estimable at all, and a calibration showing that here it is not -- so channels must be priced one at a time and never added up. Pre-registration protects against choosing a statistic after seeing the data, not against choosing one that cannot be read; we report two such, from one frozen pipeline of 4317 controlled interventions. The first is a mediated fraction, whose two estimators are treated as interchangeable. They differ by exactly $E[r(M) | A]-E[r(M) | B]$, for $r$ the residual of the conditional mean after its linear projection, bounded by $osc(r)d_{TV}$, and agree for every pair of exposure laws iff that conditional mean is affine (Prop. [prop:routes]) -- so they disagree most where the product route is the only one computable. Here they disagree by 75.0 points and our frozen verdict had silently picked one. Which is readable is settled empirically: injecting a known mediated fraction into the real mediator, the estimator's reading covers 12.9% and 28.7% of the range the truth covers and returns +131.4% and -842.5% at total mediation. Published guidance clears us on both its thresholds and the quantity that governs is not in it. Put at risk on 416 designed protein binders the bound does not merely hold, it tracks: overlap differs across the two corpora by 2.72 and the route gap by 2.66. The two channels we can price directly go opposite ways -- the designers' placement carries the effect (+0.0250 marginal against +0.0539 matched) and the free energy their programs optimised carries none (-1.9%, [-10.6%,+6.8%]) -- and what survives is stated as the bounds 58.6% and 6.8%. Every mediated fraction this work previously reported is withdrawn.

claim_quotes_as_printed.verbatim_as_printed: Proposition [prop:routes] says the two routes may disagree and says when. It does not say whether either is reporting anything. That is an empirical question about this corpus at this signal-to-noise, and it has an experiment: hold the estimator's machinery fixed and vary a truth it is supposed to recover. The first attempt failed, and its failure has a name. We built a synthetic mediator $M= 1[G--C]+eps$ and conditioned on it. That variable depends on the treatment but does not predict the outcome, so it lies on no causal path; conditioning on it destroys overlap between the arms without shrinking the within-stratum contrast. At $$ large the matched weight fell to zero and the run recorded a detection. It had detected overlap collapse. The mediator is Definition [def:dg]: the free energy the model itself assigns to the individual pair. Every program in the corpus optimises a sum of such terms, so holding this quantity fixed holds fixed what the design loop was told about the pair. Stratification, and the overlap it needs. $Delta G_{loc}$ is cut at fixed quantiles of the pooled distribution -- $5$ bins, edges fixed once, before any contrast -- and the bin index joins $(design,depth,crossed)$ in the stratum. Because the edges do not depend on the labels, permuting labels cannot rebuild the matched set, which is what Prop. [prop:null] requires. claim_quotes_as_printed.verbatim_as_printed: A proposition proved on a page and exercised on the corpus that motivated it has been checked against itself. Proposition [prop:routes] makes a claim with no RNA in it -- it is about a treatment, a mediator and a stratification -- so it can be put at risk somewhere this paper's apparatus has no purchase. We ran it on a corpus of designed protein binders: 416 records over 6 target-by-method cells for IL7Ra, InsulinR, TrkA, with binder hydrophobicity as the treatment, chain length as the mediator, and measured binding as the outcome. Nothing about base pairs, helices, folding models or chemical probing survives the transfer. The premise transfers first, which is why the rest is readable: the method a binder came from explains $^2=0.2594$ of the mediator within a target (0.1710 to 0.4203 across the three), the same producer-preference structure this paper documents for RNA. claim_quotes_as_printed.verbatim_as_printed: Two facts about the corpus set the scale for everything below, and neither is a test. Where the variance is. Decomposing the design score gives $28.8%$ between targets, $24.1%$ between methods within target, and $47.1%$ within cell, of which $15.1%$ is measurement noise. This is an identity, not a hypothesis, and it is why every estimator in this paper is computed after centring within $(target,method)$: the first two layers are removed by construction rather than adjusted for. How much of the within-cell variance is reproducible at all. The release contains $557$ groups of repeated measurements covering $1983$ rows. This is the one interval in the paper that resamples something other than targets: its unit of replication is the repeated measurement group, as section [sec:preregprotocol] notes. independence_conditions: Do not import, call or execute any module under rna_harness/. The result track must not run the audited party's implementation.
Do not take any number in claims.json:printed_value as an input. Those are the claims under audit, supplied so you know what to disagree with.
The two public CSVs in artifacts.json:input_data are the substrate. Everything else in this repository is OUR output and is evidence about our process, not evidence for a number.
Derive your own supervision plan. sanity_checks.md lists first-principles invariants this manuscript asserts; they are claims to be checked, not a plan to be adopted.
